tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description begins with 'Use when...' which is imperative phrasing directing the agent. It focuses on observable symptoms/user intent (input loss, dropped frames, fill/black frames, active alerts, output errors, pipeline desync, schedule anomalies) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists trigger contexts, and also carves out boundaries (what it's NOT for), which helps routing. It is a longer paragraph but proportionate to the complexity/scope of the skill, and remains focused and information-dense rather than padded.
tests.evidence: "Deep investigation of a single AWS Elemental MediaLive channel. Use when a customer reports a MediaLive problem or when evidence points at the encoding layer: input loss, dropped frames, fill or black frames in output, active alerts, output 4xx/5xx push errors, pipeline desynchronization on STANDARD channels, or schedule and input-switch anomalies..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but entirely domain-specific: CLI commands, metric names, decision trees, and MediaLive-specific behavior. It does not explain general concepts the agent would already know (e.g., what CloudWatch is, what a channel is in general terms); it jumps straight into MediaLive-specific procedures and non-obvious facts.
tests.evidence: FillMsec measures the duration of inserted fill/black frames in the output, capped at 60,000 ms (1 minute). After the cap, the metric stays at 60,000 until it drops to zero.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
